A U.S. Department of Energy electrical engineer has been arrested for allegedly trying to support Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.
Prosecutors say Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy, 51, bought chemicals used in homemade explosives and drone parts, traveled to Yemen, and provided advice on communications equipment. The FBI says he was smuggled into Yemen and hoped to build government-level contacts with the Houthis.
He is charged with providing material support to a U.S.-designated foreign terrorist organization.
Source: AP

events.text: Explosions are reported in Russia’s Moscow region near the Krasnozavodsk Chemical Plant, a key Russian special-chemicals enterprise specializing in pyrotechnics, ammunition and explosives. According to available information, the facility is also involved in developing and manufacturing thermobaric warheads for Shahed, or Geran, strike UAVs.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: Russia launched 97 attack drones at Ukraine during the day on October 1, including 66 jet-powered UAVs and Gerbera drones. Ukrainian air defenses downed or suppressed 78 of the incoming drones, including 55 of the jet-powered targets.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: Ukraine’s Air Force confirmed the loss of a MiG-29 and its pilot during a combat mission on October 1. Capt. Marat Mambetov, 25, a flight commander with the 40th Tactical Aviation Brigade “Ghost of Kyiv,” was conducting missile and bomb strikes against Russian forces when his aircraft was hit by a Russian missile. Mambetov ejected from the fighter but did not survive, according to the Air Force.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: President Zelensky ordered an urgent review of agreements with partners covering ammunition for Ukraine’s F-16s and missiles for air defense. An updated delivery schedule for every country, agreement and package is due tomorrow. Zelensky said some commitments already agreed with foreign leaders have not yet been implemented at command level and stressed that additional missiles are needed in October. He thanked Germany, Norway and Finland for moving quickly.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: Ukraine’s SkyFall unveiled Thor Hammer, its first middle-strike UAV, with variants offering ranges of up to 350 km and 600 km. Already used on the battlefield, it carries a 40-50 kg warhead, reaches 180 km/h and costs $25,000-30,000 depending on configuration. An operator makes the final decision to strike, after which AI and computer vision automatically correct the flight path, with guidance continuing even if radio or video communication is lost.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: Russia is producing around 2,000 jet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones per month, RBC-Ukraine reports. Production reportedly increased after Russia ended Geran-3 production and redirected components to newer models, while further scaling is constrained by turbojet engines supplied from China. The outlet also reported that Russia may have held around 10,000 conventional piston-powered strike drones in stock as of last week.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: Russian sources report increasing Ukrainian activity on the Russian-held left bank of the Dnipro in Kherson region. They claim Ukrainian assault groups are repeatedly operating around the destroyed Antonivskyi Bridge and the nearby Dachi settlement, seeking conditions to establish a foothold. The reports say Ukrainian forces maintain constant aerial reconnaissance and extensively use FPV drones to isolate the area, with the situation changing rapidly.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: A drone struck a school in Kyiv’s Solomianskyi district, damaging the facade of the educational building at third-floor level and starting a fire, according to police. No casualties were initially reported. At the time of the attack, more than 100 students and around 60 school employees were inside a shelter.

He did liken this incident to the 9/11, arguing that the people onboard of the aircraft managed to prevent an airplane crash similar to those that occurred during those terrorist attacks.
The Israeli prime minister also compared the incident to action movies, describing it as “Hollywood on steroids” during another interview on Fox News.
